_comment: T-592, proposals for the playtest (Level design, Decisions, "Needle routes"). How a route's pairs show in a run: the dashed line of the active pair (the one that pays) is drawn bright and a little thicker, so the eye finds the next gap from a distance; the route's waiting pairs are drawn faint, still there so the player can read the route, but clearly not the target. A pair in no route keeps T-272's look (alpha 0.35, width 1). waiting_threaded "nothing": threading a waiting pair pays no trick, makes no flash and does not move the route on, so only the bright gap matters and a route can't be skipped by threading its pairs out of order. random_start "random": a random route starts at a random pair (an in-order route starts at its first), so two runs of the same level differ from the first gap.
